_comment: The ONLY npm packages ContentForge will ever tell anyone to run with npx. An entry here means the package is published by the vendor of the service itself: the npm publisher is the vendor's account and the repository is the vendor's own. Everything else is 'no verified connector': connector setup prints the options (the vendor's own MCP server, an HTTP aggregator, or skipping) and never writes a command or environment variables for it. Add a package only after checking all three of: the npm maintainer account belongs to the vendor, the repository is the vendor's, and the vendor's own documentation names this package. Every entry carries an exact `version` (the newest release at least 14 days old): a command is always `name@version`, never a bare name, so a later malicious release cannot reach anyone who has not been given a new pin. scripts/npm_allowlist.py checks this file offline (every runnable package must be listed) and online (every listed package still exists, still has versions, and still has the expected publisher); a weekly workflow runs the online check.
